q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a bottle of shampoo?
title: Shampoo carbon footprint per bottle
short: Add the surfactants, water and additives per bottle and the plastic bottle and cap, each with supplier figures. Add mixing, filling and labelling energy, then divide the plant's energy by bottles filled, stated by volume.
audience: Shampoo makers and personal care brands

ul: Plastic bottle and cap, or sachet film.
Mixing tanks, with heating if required.
Air conditioning and lighting for the line.

p: Report per bottle with its volume. Sachets and large bottles carry very different pack weight per millilitre.

example.title: Worked example: shampoo unit per bottle (one month)
lines: Plant total: 18,300 / 500,000 = 0.0366 kg CO2 per bottle
Add ingredients and bottle for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
